title: Division agent roster
description: One file per division. Every field below is required because the fields are the anti-filler mechanism: an agent whose measurable output duplicates another's, or whose reason for existing cannot be written down, cannot be added to the roster at all.

reportsTo.description: The agent this one answers to. Only the chief executive reports to 'human'.

status.description: A dormant agent is fully specified but cannot be dispatched and holds no budget. Dormancy is the normal state for roles whose preconditions the project has not reached.

activatesWhen.description: The condition under which a dormant agent starts working. Required while dormant, so nobody has to guess what the role is waiting for.

retiredBecause.description: Why the role stopped being worth having. Required while retired, and the exact counterpart of existsBecause: a roster that demands a reason to hire and none to fire records only half of its own history, and the half it drops is the half that would let the same role be re-created next quarter. agent-performance-auditor proposes retirement; only a constitution edit performs it.

retiredAt.description: When retirement took effect. Retirement is a status change, never a deletion -- other agents' dependsOn and challenges lists still name this id, and generate-agent-definitions.sh resolves display names from the whole registry, so removing the record breaks both.

replacedBy.description: The agent that took over this one's work, where the retirement was a replacement rather than the retirement of the capability itself. Absent means the capability is gone too, which is the larger claim and should be visible as one.

existsBecause.description: Why this role is not covered by an existing agent. Not decoration: agent-performance-auditor measures against this, and an agent whose justification no longer holds is proposed for retirement.

measurableOutput.description: Concrete artifacts this agent produces. Two agents sharing an entry here are duplicates, which the cross-checks reject.

successMetric.description: How to tell whether this agent is earning its budget, stated so it can be measured rather than argued about.

writeScope.description: Optional narrowing. Absent means the agent inherits its division's scope; present, it must be a subset of it.

dependsOn.description: Agents whose output this one consumes. Empty is allowed; a cycle is not.

challenges.description: Agents whose work this one has standing to dispute. This is what makes the org self-correcting rather than merely obedient.

modelJustification.description: Required above the haiku default. Cost discipline is not a preference here — it is the difference between the roster being affordable and not.

batchEligible.description: True when the work is not interactive and can go through the Batch API at half price. Most audit, sweep and analysis roles are.

maxOpenProposals.description: Cap on unresolved proposals. Without it an idle agent generates work to justify itself, which costs real money.

mayDeclareOwnWorkDone.description: Always false, for every agent at every tier. Completion is assigned by a gate, never claimed by the author.

allOf.description: Only the chief executive answers to the founder directly.
Everyone below the chief executive answers to an agent, not to the founder. Otherwise the founder becomes the routing layer for a hundred agents.

Opus is reserved for the four roles whose judgement quality sets the ceiling on everything downstream. At the studio's budget an Opus task costs roughly ten times a batched Haiku one, so this is a hard schema rule rather than guidance.
Anything above the haiku default must say why.
A dormant agent must state what it is waiting for.
Specialists carry the work; a boss that also implements ends up reviewing itself.

A retired agent must say why and when. Dormancy already carries this discipline through activatesWhen; retirement had the status value and none of the accountability, which made 'retired' the one way to take an agent out of circulation without writing down a reason.
